Cannabidiol supplements (CBD) are increasingly consumed by athletes to improve regeneration. However, the evidence for the pro-regenerative effects of CBD in sports is quite limited. Therefore, our aim was to investigate the effects of a single CBD supplementation in a six-arm placebo-controlled crossover study after resistance training on performance and muscle damage. Before and after the resistance training, one-repetition maximum in the back squat (1RM BS), countermovement jump (CMJ), and blood serum concentrations of creatine kinase (CK) and myoglobin (Myo) were measured in healthy, well-trained participants. 16 out of 21 participants completed the study and were included in the analysis. In 1RM BS, a significant decrease was observed after 24 h ( p < 0.01) but not after 48 and 72 h. A significant group difference was detected after 72 h ( p < 0.05; ES = 0.371). In CMJ, no significant changes were observed. The CK and Myo concentrations increased significantly after 24 h (CK: p < 0.001; Myo: p < 0.01), 48 h (CK: p < 0.001; Myo: p < 0.01) and 72 h (CK: p < 0.001; Myo: p < 0.001). After 72 h, significant group differences were observed for both muscle damage biomarkers (CK: p < 0.05 ES = 0.24; Myo: p < 0.05; ES = 0.21). The results show small but significant effects on muscle damage and recovery of squat performance after 72 h. However, more data are required for clearer statements concerning potential pro-regenerative effects of CBD supplementation after resistance training. cannabidiol CBD recovery muscle damage performance strength training resistance training 1. Introduction Intense training and performance result in damage and inflammation of the skeletal muscles [ 1 , 2 , 3 ]. Consequently, the performance of the trained skeletal muscles decreases after the intensive training sessions and needs time to recover [ 4 , 5 , 6 ]. In competitive sports, it is essential to minimise recovery time in order to provide further training stimuli as quick as possible and thus to increase performance. Dietary supplements are often used to this end [ 7 , 8 , 9 ]. Cannabidiol (CBD) products in particular are often consumed by elite athletes [ 10 , 11 , 12 ]. CBD is a non-psychoactive compound of Cannabis sativa [ 13 ]. Due to its structural differences to ∆ 9 -tetrahydrocannabinol (∆ 9 -THC), CBD has different affinities to cannabinoid receptors 1 and 2 [ 14 , 15 , 16 , 17 ]. Mechanistically, CBD can inhibit the NF- κ B signaling pathway and activate JAK/STAT kinase [ 18 ]. Therefore, CBD is used in a variety of diseases such as autoimmune encephalitis [ 19 ], rheumatoid arthritis [ 20 ], colitis [ 21 ], diabetes [ 22 ], and psoriasis [ 23 ], as well as Alzheimer’s [ 24 ], Parkinson’s [ 25 ], and Huntington’s Disease [ 26 ]. It has also anticonvulsant [ 14 , 27 , 28 , 29 ], antipsychotic [ 14 , 27 , 30 ], antiemetic [ 14 , 27 ], anticarcinogenic [ 31 , 32 ], and antidepressant [ 14 , 33 ] effects. Although regulations regarding its legality vary among countries worldwide [ 34 , 35 ], CBD was removed from the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) prohibited substances list in 2018 [ 36 ], based on evidence that CBD is safe and well-tolerated by humans [ 37 , 38 , 39 ]. While the effects and associated mechanisms of CBD in the human body have been studied [ 40 , 41 , 42 ], data in the context of sports and performance is still limited. Previous research has shown that roughly 27–42% of CBD users report improvement of sleep as reason for administration [ 43 , 44 ]. Improved sleep quality has been shown mainly in animal models [ 45 , 46 ] and not clearly in humans [ 47 , 48 , 49 ]. Additionally, first studies have shown a small effect on muscle soreness after CBD supplementation [ 50 , 51 ]. Concerning pro-regenerative effects of CBD in sport, currently only two studies exist which investigated biomarkers and performance parameters. In untrained males, the intake of CBD oil after six sets of ten maximal eccentric isokinetic elbow flexions did not result in any significant differences in perceived soreness, arm circumference, hanging joint angle, and peak torque between the groups [ 51 ]. In contrast, a pilot study [ 52 ] in highly trained men (>150% of body weight in the back squat [ 53 ]), showed an inhibitory effect of CBD on serum creatine kinase (CK) concentrations after three sets of 12 back squats at 70% 1RM plus three sets of 15 drop jumps landed in a deep squat. Consequently, based on the current lack of data, no definite conclusion can be drawn concerning the effects of CBD supplementation to promote regeneration processes after intensive strength training. Therefore, the aim of this study was to investigate the effects of a single CBD supplementation 24, 48, and 72 h after intensive strength training on muscle damage and performance. For this purpose, a placebo-controlled, double-blind, six-arm crossover study was conducted.

extracted_data.document_summary: This placebo-controlled, double-blind, six-arm crossover study investigated the effects of a single 60 mg Cannabidiol (CBD) supplementation versus placebo after an intensive resistance training protocol (designed to induce muscle damage) on skeletal muscle regeneration and performance in healthy, well-trained participants. The study measured muscle damage biomarkers (Creatine Kinase and Myoglobin) and neuromuscular performance (1RM Back Squat and Countermovement Jump) at 24, 48, and 72 hours post-training. While overall effects were small, CBD significantly attenuated increases in CK and Myo concentrations and aided in the recovery of 1RM Back Squat performance after 72 hours, but showed no significant effect on Countermovement Jump performance.

treatment_details.therapy_type: Cannabidiol (CBD) supplementation following an intensive strength training protocol.
treatment_details.dose_specificity:
Participants underwent an intensive strength training protocol consisting of three sets of 12 back squats at 70% of 1RM with 150 seconds rest, and three sets of 15 drop jumps from a 45 cm box landed in a deep squat with 60 seconds rest. A single dose of 60 mg CBD solubilisat or a placebo drink was consumed directly after exercise, with effects monitored at 24, 48, and 72 hours post-training. Absolute strength values and training loads averaged 118.6 
± 22.6 kg. The study did not include dose-response comparisons for CBD, nor did it investigate chronic supplementation or endurance training effects, and it was suggested that the protocol might not have induced sufficient power reduction for CMJ.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: initially decreased, then recovered and increased
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Significant decrease observed after 24 h (p < 0.01) in both groups; significant group difference detected after 72 h (p < 0.05; ES = 0.371), with the CBD group recovering and slightly increasing performance. Overall, a significant increase over the course of the study (p < 0.05, ES = 0.34), representing a linear recovery trend.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Measures maximal muscular strength in a single effort, reflecting lower body muscular strength and adaptation to strength training.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Post-intensive resistance training (including back squats) with single CBD or placebo supplementation, measured at 24, 48, and 72 hours during recovery.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates recovery of squat performance and muscle function post-exercise; CBD appears to support the recovery of maximal strength performance after 72 hours following intensive exercise.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: No significant changes observed at any time or over the course of the study, and no significant differences between groups.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Indicator of explosive lower body power and neuromuscular function, reflecting the ability to rapidly produce force and height in a vertical jump.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: After intensive resistance training and single CBD supplementation, compared to placebo, measured at 24, 48, and 72 hours during recovery.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates an individual's explosive muscular power and readiness for explosive movements. The lack of observed change suggests that either the training protocol did not induce sufficient power reduction or the test might not be ideal for this specific outcome.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Initially elevated, then decreased over study course; CBD attenuated the increase and showed lower levels.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly after 24 h (p < 0.001), 48 h (p < 0.001), and 72 h (p < 0.001) in both groups. CBD attenuated the increase after 72 h, resulting in a significant group difference (p < 0.05; ES = -0.24). Significant negative population trends were observed with an effect size of -0.29; comparably small. The CBD group largely recovered after 72 hours.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Enzyme primarily found in muscle cells, involved in energy metabolism. Elevated levels in serum are a marker of skeletal muscle damage and breakdown.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: Following an intensive resistance training protocol and single CBD supplementation, measured at 24, 48, and 72 hours post-training, compared to placebo.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates the level of muscle damage or injury. Higher levels suggest greater exercise-induced muscle damage. CBD may aid in the recovery from muscle damage after 72 hours by attenuating the increase.

measured_effect.direction_of_change: Initially increased, then decreased over study course; CBD dampened the increase and showed lower levels.
measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly after 24 h (p < 0.01), 48 h (p < 0.01), and 72 h (p < 0.001) in both groups. CBD showed a dampening effect on ln (Myo) after 72 h, resulting in a significant group difference (p < 0.05; ES = 0.21). Significant negative population trends observed with an effect size of -0.25; comparably small. The CBD group largely recovered after 72 hours.
